decision: Run one bounded bare hardware canary after both shared queue lanes are free. Use --kds off --registry off.
basis: Read run-canary.py, verify-canary.mjs, owner-config.mjs and qemu-restrict.sh; reviewed recipe and frozen inputs
4096 MiB SNP guest; 6144 MiB isolated scope; no app, funding, registry, guestd, relay, platform API or MCP action
Slirp restrict=on and exactly one ephemeral loopback 8444 forward; no registry private key provided
Real verifier requires hardware, expected measurement, config, attested TLS key, supervisor key and exact runtime checks
Signals scoped to owned pid/starttime identities and unique transient unit; production QEMU identities checked before/after
requiredActualRunEvidence: terminal cgroup must be observed and empty, not merely unknown
every protected QEMU identity and enclave service identity unchanged
child result ok and all required acceptance checks true
private directory absent and no run-owned survivor
limitations: The canary is intentionally unregistered; registry remains pending, not fake verified
No claim of native TLS additions, platform API or MCP readiness; this image is the earlier 6f candidate
Root will inspect actual terminal evidence before accepting hardware result
